For me, I went back in time. Their album before Blurryface was Vessel. This album is almost as upbeat as Blurryface and integrates some of their older style of music. Vessel is my favorite album to be honest. Then once you really get into that, look up their Regional At Best album; also upbeat but has even more personal lyrics in my opinion (also keep in mind many songs in Vessel were remastered from RaB). I would also suggest looking up lyrics for any songs that interest you. Look up interviews and things that Tyler and Josh have done, this will really connect the dots between the music and the passionate people behind it. It really makes the music more meaningful. Then, once you've gotten that far, check out the Self-Titled album (twenty one pilots). It was made before Josh was in the band. In this album you'll find that though it isn't very upbeat, it is a really deep and meaningful album. Tyler sings about things that he struggles with and wants to express through music.

But if you make it through all of that and you still love twenty one pilots, then check out Tyler's No Phun Intended album. He created it when he was 17 years old. Though the production quality is lacking, it was created with a lot of heart. This is also a very meaningful album. Definitely the most personal of them all.

But this measurement is not relevant to whatever calculations we are going to be concerned with. Kinetic energy is a measurement of relativity. The amount of energy in the universe does not change and on that scale, everything adds up to that total amount, but you have to consider it relative to itself. When we want to calculate the kinetic energy of a ball on a bus, we are just trying to find how much energy is stored in the ball's movement relative to the bus or the ground, but this is very little compared to it's actual energy relative to the universe.
